News.title: ‘High-risk’ victim of freed grooming gang ringleader is given police protection as she blasts ‘I’m scared for my safety’
News.content:
UNDER GUARD ‘High-risk’ victim of freed grooming gang ringleader is given police protection as she blasts ‘I’m scared for my safety’

A VICTIM of the Rochdale grooming gang ringleader has been given police protection following his release.

Shabir Ahmed, 73, walked out of HMP Leeds on licence this week after serving just 14 years of a 22-year-sentence.





Now, it has been revealed that a victim of the Rochdale grooming gang has been provided with additional security at her home, reports The Times.

The victim, named only as Ruby, was 12 when the abuse started and said she had been plied with vodka and cigarettes before being raped “continuously” by up to 40 men.

Officers from Greater Manchester Police are now reportedly treating her as a “high risk victim”.

The force have given her an “urgent response marker” which allows rapid deployment to her home following Ahmed’s release on Thursday.



Last week, Ruby – who is now 32 – met senior officers who were told she “does not feel safe with Ahmed in the community”.

She has also been provided with an app on her phone which she can use to alert police should she feel threatened or in danger.

The Sun previously reported how Ahmed was deemed “unsafe” to be released and a “high risk” to children before he was freed from prison.

The former taxi driver, who forced his victims to call him “Daddy”, will now be heavily monitored by the authorities.



Ruby had already been forced to come face-to-face with one of her attackers while in a local shop after he was released from jail halfway through his sentence – but the victim was not informed.

Maggie Oliver resigned from her role as detective constable with GMP in 2012 after bringing the failure of authorities to light.

She said that she met with GMP last week to ensure Ruby had security in place at her home in Rochdale as “none of that was done for her”.

“She’s been set up now for her safety. She’s in a mess. She’s fearful, and rightly so. She’s been threatened at gunpoint, her and Amber, and told not to go to the police. That man was never prosecuted,” she said.

“Amber”, not her real name, was raped and sexually exploited by Ahmed.



She said in a statement: “I am absolutely furious that no one contacted me to tell me that Shabir Ahmed was going to be released – not the Prison Service, not Victim Liaison, no one.”

It is understood that other victims have seen their security stepped up after Ahmed’s release but Oliver says many had not been told he had been freed.

Meanwhile, some have also told The Sunday Times that they “have no idea” where they’re abusers live and had not been in touch with authorities for years.

Victims of the paedophile ring, including Ruby, were also promised Ahmed would be deported after he was released from prison.

However, due to a loophole in the Immigration Act 1971, Ahmed is set to stay in the country despite having his British citizenship removed.



The Act forbids the removal of a small group of Commonwealth citizens who arrived in the UK more than 50 years ago.

Home Secretary, Shabana Mahmood, is planning to scrap the legal loophole stopping Ahmed from being deported.

Meanwhile, the government is said to be considering imposing tough visa sanctions or withholding foreign aid to force Pakistan to take back Ahmed.

But The Telegraph reports that Ahmed cannot be deported after he renounced his Pakistani citizenship.

As a result, Pakistani officials are refusing to have him returned to their country, claiming he is no longer a citizen.



The leader of the paedophile gang was jailed for 22 years in 2012 after being convicted of two counts of rape, one sex assault, trafficking and conspiracy to engage in sexual activity with a child.

He plied girls as young as 13 with drink and drugs before abusing them with eight of his friends.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

During his trial, he exposed his naked torso in the dock and threw a clump of chest hair on the floor, saying of one victim: “She would have seen this.”

Following his release, he will now be housed in a bail hostel in the north of England, costing the taxpayer an estimated £120 a night.

News.title: Andy Burnham’s adviser called for Royal Family to be scaled back and to return some of their wealth
News.content:
ONE of Andy Burnham’s key advisers said the Royal Family ought to be scaled back and should return some of their wealth.

MP Miatta Fahnbulleh said the monarchy’s fortune “belongs to us”.





She argued the royals should be financially independent, suggesting an end to the taxpayer-funded Sovereign Grant which supports official duties.

Ms Fahnbulleh said in 2020: “I think the monarchy needs to be reformed.

“For me, that means constitutional reform — so we’re no longer a nation of subjects but a nation of citizens — through to [scaling it down] so there are less royals.

“And the fact we have this very wealthy family that should be financially independent.

“Wealth they have accumulated through centuries, they should be giving some back to the public because in the end it belongs to us.”

She made the comments on BBC show Question Time when she was chief of think-tank New Economics Foundation.

She is now the MP for Peckham in South East London.

Mr Burnham may become PM in two weeks.



Alex Burghart, Shadow Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, said: “The King of the North and his team already have their sights set on our actual King.

“Labour is about to hold its own coronation — and the man taking the crown is putting the future of the monarchy in doubt.”

Ms Fahnbulleh, Mr Burnham and Labour were asked to comment.

News.title: Fury as Labour hands out £180m to firms to employ youngsters instead of cutting crippling business rates
News.content:
LABOUR has been blasted for handing £180m to companies to employ youngsters – instead of cutting crippling business rates.

Employers can claim £3,000 for every long-term unemployed young person they hire.





The scheme aims to help 60,000 people aged 18-24 into work over the next three years in a bid to tackle the youth jobs crisis.

However, critics point out Labour’s policy decisions like hiking employers’ national insurance contributions and increasing minimum wage have added to the crisis.

“Labour’s youth job subsidy is a complete sham,” Helen Whately, Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary, blasted.

“Money that could be put towards tax cuts is being dished out with no guarantee it will go towards creating any new jobs.”



The scheme will not create new roles and the grants can be pocketed by the companies involved.

Ms Whately added: “The Government has admitted they won’t be able to tell what the money has been spent on.

“This is a desperate attempt to patch up the damage they have done to opportunities for young people with their jobs tax and employment rights bill. They have killed jobs and created a lost generation.

“Only the Conservatives understand that businesses need government to get out of the way so they can create the jobs the country sorely needs.”



Nearly one million people aged 16 to 24 are not in employment, education or training.

A spokesperson for the Department for Work and Pensions said: “Every employer participating in the Youth Jobs Grant must meet robust conditions, with funding only released once employment has been verified.

“The scheme will support up to 60,000 young people to take the first step in their career, which we know is vital to securing their long-term employment.

“It is part of our £2.5 billion drive to help almost a million young people towards work.”

News.title: Birds in Ukraine are weaving ‘apocalyptic’ nests out of fibre-optic drone cables on the frontline
News.content:
CYBER NESTS Birds in Ukraine are weaving ‘apocalyptic’ nests out of fibre-optic drone cables on the frontline

BIRDS living along Ukraine’s war-torn front line are building apocalyptic nests from discarded fibre-optic cables used to guide attack drone swarms.

Multiple nests woven with a mixture of grass, twigs, and the ultra-thin wires have sparked debate about how the brutal four-year conflict is reshaping nature.





Giant spider webs of the fibre-optic cables, used by both Ukraine and Russia to make drones resistant to electronic jamming, now cover large stretches of the 746-mile front line.

Vladimir Putin launched his “special military operation” against Ukraine in February 2022 with tanks, armoured vehicles and artillery.

Since then, drones have become a dominant feature of the battlefield, with both sides increasingly reliant on them in combat.

The growing use of fibre-optic drones has left cables scattered across the landscape, where birds appear to be adapting to the new reality around them.

The abandoned cables can be found draped across rooftops, tangled in trees and strewn through fields.

Ukrainian troops have shared photos and videos of nests woven from dry grass and fibre-optic cable across battle-scarred regions including Donetsk, Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia.

Olena Tregub, secretary general of the Ukrainian civil society group, NAKO, called the creations “apocalyptic”.

Yana Hrynko, a senior researcher at Kyiv’s War Museum, has examined two such nests sent from the front line by Ukrainian troops.



She said: “Bird nests with fragments of optic fibre demonstrate the change in the nature of war.

“The first nest mainly contains dry grass and fibre-optic cable. And it’s pretty tightly twisted.”

Hrynko said researchers do not yet know which species built the nests or how the birds gathered the cables, which can stretch for more than 12 miles.



One nest was reportedly found after a Russian glide bomb knocked down a tree in Donbas.

A support battalion of Ukraine’s 12th Azov Brigade shared an image of a nest on Telegram last month.

The brigade said: “This is just one of dozens of manifestations of how nature survives in the flames of war.

“Between hundreds of drones, assaults, shelling, and kilometres of scorched earth.”

The unusual nests have attracted attention from researchers beyond Ukraine.



One of the two nests will remain in Kyiv as part of the War Museum’s collection, while the other is being sent to the Netherlands for further study before being returned.

Auke-Florian Hiemstra, a biologist based in the Dutch city of Leiden who specialises in artificial nest materials, said testing could reveal which bird species built the nests.

She said: “We’re going to look for DNA traces still in a nest to determine who actually made the nest.

“I have never seen nests like this before – and I have seen many, many bird nests.”

Hiemstra said the impact of fibre-optic cables on birds could be both positive and negative.



While birds could become tangled in the material, the cables may also help create stronger nests.

She said: “And by documenting this nest, we’re also documenting the impact of war on nature in Ukraine.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Birds are often choosy about what they pluck for nests, but have been speculated to employ ingenious tactics – such as using snakeskin and toxic cigarette butts to ward off predators.

Researchers say that the animals are increasingly using everyday human rubbish to make nests.

News.title: Star-studded gigs, Red Arrows flypast & message from King – How USA celebrated 250 years of independence
News.content:
THE United States ­partied hard celebrating its 250th birthday ­yesterday — as King Charles paid tribute to the nation’s “remarkable” history.

Celebrations went on across the country with landmarks and people decorated in Stars and Stripes flags — despite a heatwave forcing events to be axed.





President Donald Trump had kicked off the festivities on Friday with a speech at Mount Rushmore — as well as posting an image online depicting his own face on the landmark of famous presidents.

Charles, who visited the US in April with Queen Camilla, congratulated the President and hailed the countries’ bond — following its move to independence from us in 1776.

He wrote in an online post: “Our nations have built a relationship founded on friendship, trust and a belief in liberty, the rule of law and the dignity of all people.

“As we look ahead to the next 250 years, I have no doubt we will continue to defend our shared values.



“The connection between our peoples is one that I trust will only grow stronger with time.”

Another UK tribute came from the RAF’s Red Arrows display team with a flypast over New York.

President Trump had appeared for 30 minutes at Mount Rushmore and spoke of his fear of a “communist menace” in the country from progressive Democrats.

He said: “We will send them quickly away, and we will continue to build our country bigger and better, stronger than ever before. America will never be a communist country!”



He had paid tribute to ­former US presidents George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and ­Abraham Lincoln — whose faces are carved on the historic ­landmark in South Dakota.

But he also posted on Truth Social an image showing a gold depiction of the sculpture — with his own face as a fifth head on it.

Mr Trump was due yesterday to give another speech during a rally at the National Mall in Washington DC — where the Washington Monument had been lit up since Friday.



Proud Americans took the chance to dress up to mark the milestone anniversary.

Yanks in the UK were seen celebrating, with one woman dressed up as a cowgirl in ­Tooting, South London.



Fans attending the World Cup match in Houston between Morocco and Canada wore fancy dress and brought ­birthday banners with them.

A six-hour concert was scheduled in Philadelphia, with stars including Christina ­Aguilera, Will Smith and Seal due to perform.

The glittering Times Square ball, ­which usually drops down a pole to mark New Year, was lowered eight times to mark the start of ­Independence Day in every US timezone and overseas territory.



In Los Angeles, rapper Queen Latifah hosted a concert featuring The Smashing Pumpkins, Chris Stapleton and Chaka Khan.

But severe heat — with ­predicted temperatures of 39C (102F) — forced several other event organisers across the country to change and even cancel festivities.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A parade in Washington was cancelled, while the Great American State Fair in the city started two hours late.

Other major cities expanded cooling centres and shortened parade routes to protect people from the searing sun.

News.title: Andy Burnham’s ‘German plan’ will hammer South with higher taxes and leave Britain poorer, critics warn
News.content:
ANDY Burnham’s “German” plan for Britain will mean higher taxes and no growth, senior MPs have warned.

The Prime Minister-in-waiting called for “equivalent living conditions” across the country in his big speech this week.





But there are fears the idea, based on the German constitution, will hammer the South and set regions against each other.

Shadow Chancellor Sir Mel Stride said the blueprint focuses too much on “redistribution” instead of growth.

He said: “Burnham seems obsessed with how the pie is divided rather than making the pie larger.

“Of course we need higher growth in those areas which have not been thriving. But that should not come at the expense of higher taxes on other parts of the country. That approach ends up being self-defeating.”



Reform UK’s Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said: “We need to lift all parts of the country up, not pit them against each other. To get the country back on track, Burnham should start by cutting appalling waste of taxpayer’s money.”

Mr Burnham, who watched his rugby league side Leigh Leopards beat Warrington Wolves yesterday, aims to create a Downing Street team in Manchester — dubbed No 10 North — to “redistribute power and resources across the UK”.

In his leadership speech, he said it will “strive for equivalent living conditions in all parts of Britain — borrowing from the German Basic Law.”

Meanwhile The Sun on Sunday can reveal if England win the World Cup, Mr Burnham’s allies want a victory parade in Manchester — even though plans are under way in London for after July 19’s final.



But one Labour MP said: “What better way to show the country they have reason to hope again.”

And referring to a suburb of Manchester, another joked: “Let’s bring it Hulme”.

The Government as already announced its intention to bid for the North of England to host the Olympics in the 2040s.

News.title: Girl, 11, ‘accidentally shot in the head by McDonald’s worker’ as her family picked up food
News.content:
HORRIFIC ACCIDENT Girl, 11, ‘accidentally shot in the head by McDonald’s worker’ as her family picked up food

AN ELEVEN-YEAR-OLD girl was accidentally shot in the head by a McDonald’s worker as her family picked up their order.

Dora Belen Rivera was sat in a car parked outside waiting for her food when a bullet came flying out of nowhere.





Her dad, Oscar Roman Miron, was struck in the hip while her two siblings, two and five, were unharmed in the ordeal.

In the aftermath of the attack, Dora was rushed to hospital where she underwent emergency surgery.

Doctors were unable to remove bullet, according to a GoFundMe set up by the family.

It has since been revealed the family were not the intended target of employee Ralph N-Kosi Blue III, who shot someone running toward him while on the way to his shift.



The 18-year-old reportedly fired the weapon after getting into an altercation in the parking lot.

He has since been charged with two counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and two counts of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without the intent to kill.



Hallandale Beach McDonald’s Owner Brad Ashlin said in a statement: “The individual reported to be involved is no longer employed at our organisation.

“We are devastated by the shooting that occurred outside our restaurant this past weekend.”

He continued: “Our thoughts are with the father and young daughter who were injured, as well as their family during this difficult time.”

An arrest report obtained by NBC Miami said people had come to the fast-food chain two days earlier looking for Blue – who was hiding in the back.

CCTV footage on the day of the incident showed a man running after Blue, and hiding on the other side of the SUV Dora and dad were sat in.



Blue is then seen raising his weapons and pulling the trigger.

Speaking for the first time since her operation, Dora expressed her gratitude to first responders who helped save her life.

“Thank you for everything,” she said.

“Thank you for the police. Thank you for the firefighters. Thank you for the doctors.

“It feels like I have another chance.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Doctors say the 11-year-old has “a long road ahead of her and will continue to require therapy”.

Her dad has been been discharged from hospital, but said the family have been traumatised by the ordeal.

News.title: Man fighting for life after being ‘repeatedly punched & stamped on by two men as he lay on ground’ outside train station
News.content:
STATION 'ASSAULT' Man fighting for life after being ‘repeatedly punched & stamped on by two men as he lay on ground’ outside train station

A MAN has allegedly been seriously assaulted after being attacked outside a train station, as cops release images of the men they want to track down.

The man is said to have been attacked by two men outside Worcester Foregate Street station just before 8pm on July 3.





During the alleged assault he was repeatedly punched and stamped on whilst he lay on the ground.

British Transport Police officers and paramedics attended the scene, and the victim was taken to a local hospital where he remains in a critical condition.

Detectives believe the men in the CCTV images may have information that could assist their ongoing investigation.

Anyone who recognises either of them is asked to text 61016 or call 0800 40 50 40, quoting reference 642 of 3 July.

Information can be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.
